question: Which Indian sprinter was stripped of her silver medal at the 2006 Asian Games due to a failed drug test?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santhi Soundarajan**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Santhi Soundarajan** is an Indian middle-distance runner who famously won the **silver medal** in the **women's 800m** race at the **2006 Asian Games** held in **Doha, Qatar**.

• She was stripped of her medal after she failed a **gender verification test** shortly after the event. The **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** disqualified her, stating that she did not possess the sexual characteristics of a woman. While the question mentions a **failed drug test**, it is widely recognized in sports history that her disqualification at the **2006 Asian Games** was due to this controversial medical eligibility test.

• **P. T. Usha** (Option 1) is one of India's greatest athletes, known as the **Payyoli Express**. She won multiple gold medals at the **1986 Seoul Asian Games** and retired long before the **2006** incident, making this option incorrect.

• **Dutee Chand** (Option 3) is another prominent Indian sprinter who faced a ban due to **hyperandrogenism** regulations in **2014**. However, she successfully challenged the ruling at the **Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS)** and was not the athlete stripped of a medal in **2006**.

• **K. M. Beenamol** (Option 4) is a celebrated Olympian and **Padma Shri** recipient who won gold in the **800m** at the **2002 Busan Asian Games**. She was not involved in any medal-stripping controversy during the **2006** games.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Santhi Soundarajan** was born in **1981** in **Kathakkurichi**, **Tamil Nadu**. She grew up in extreme poverty and used sports as a means to support her family.

• Throughout her career, she won **11 international medals** for **India** and around **50 national medals**. Her disqualification in **2006** led to a significant decline in her mental health and financial stability, at one point forcing her to work in a **brick kiln** to survive.

• In **2016**, following years of advocacy, the **Tamil Nadu government** and the **Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT)** appointed her as a permanent **athletics coach**, recognizing her contributions to the sport.

• Her case remains a landmark in the discussion of **human rights** and **gender ethics** in international sports, alongside athletes like **Caster Semenya**. It highlighted the psychological trauma caused by **sex verification** policies implemented by bodies like **World Athletics** (formerly **IAAF**).

**Important Points__**

• The **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** is the governing body for all sports in **Asia** and is responsible for organizing the **Asian Games** every **four years**.

• **Gender verification** tests were once mandatory at major sporting events but were largely abolished in the late **1990s**, only to be reintroduced on a case-by-case basis if an athlete's eligibility was questioned.

• The **2006 Doha Asian Games** saw **India** finish with a total of **53 medals**, including **10 gold**, **17 silver**, and **26 bronze**, excluding the stripped medal of **Santhi Soundarajan**.

• Current regulations by **World Athletics** focus on **testosterone** levels in female athletes with **Differences of Sexual Development (DSD)**, requiring them to medically reduce their levels to compete in certain track events.
